Unmodified third-party dependency code.

Purely a naming collision — the function never references the state variable — so it is a code-quality issue, not a logic bug.

Unmodified OZ Ownable2Step code; the two-step design (acceptOwnership must be called by the new pendingOwner) means setting newOwner to address(0) only blocks completion of that particular transfer attempt — the current owner retains ownership until acceptance, so this cannot brick or hijack ownership. Standard, low-impact, long-accepted OZ pattern.
Standard EIP-2612 permit deadline check using block.timestamp in unmodified OZ code; miner timestamp manipulation tolerance (~seconds) is immaterial to a signature-expiry deadline.

First-party validAfter/validBefore window checks in _transferOrReceiveWithAuthorization do use block.timestamp for comparisons; this is the standard, expected ERC-3009-style pattern and the small miner-manipulable drift is not a practically exploitable issue for a payment-authorization time window. Real detection, benign/low severity.

limitations: This is an independent AI adjudication, not a human review.
Static analysis cannot prove deployed governance-key custody or rule out runtime and future-upgrade risk.
